FR-001.title: The master screen MUST provide a control that opens player management in a dedicated pop-up window.

FR-002.title: The player-management pop-up MUST display every configured player's name, Intelligence level, and Hacker perk availability.

FR-003.title: The player-management pop-up MUST show a clear empty-roster state when the selected player configuration contains no players.

FR-004.title: The system MUST allow the game master to add a player only when a player configuration is selected and no broadcast is active.

FR-005.title: Adding a player MUST require a non-blank name, a whole-number Intelligence level from 1 through 10 inclusive, and an explicit Hacker perk availability choice.

FR-006.title: The system MUST store each player's Intelligence level and Hacker perk availability as part of that player's persistent roster entry.

FR-007.title: The system MUST allow the game master to change a player's name, Intelligence level, and Hacker perk availability when no broadcast is active.

FR-008.title: The system MUST allow the game master to remove a player from the roster when no broadcast is active.

FR-009.title: The system MUST reject every add, edit, or removal attempt while a broadcast is active without changing the stored roster.

FR-010.title: The player-management pop-up MUST remain available as a read-only detailed list while a broadcast is active.

FR-011.title: Editing a player's attributes MUST preserve that player's stable identity and roster position.

FR-012.title: A successful roster mutation MUST be stored before the interface reports the operation as complete.

FR-013.title: A failed roster mutation MUST leave the last stored roster unchanged and present an actionable error to the game master.

FR-014.title: Reopening a player configuration MUST restore every player's stored name, Intelligence level, Hacker perk availability, identity, and roster order.

FR-015.title: A player configuration created before this feature MUST load without manual repair by assigning Intelligence 1 and Hacker perk unavailable to entries that do not contain those attributes.

FR-016.title: Closing the player-management pop-up without submitting a roster mutation MUST leave the player configuration and current session state unchanged.

context: area: persistent player configuration and roster contracts
area: master coordination and roster-management interface
constraint: roster mutations are permitted only without an active broadcast
constraint: detailed display and editing live in a dedicated pop-up window
intent: Give the game master a safe, persistent way to manage each player's Intelligence and Hacker perk attributes in a dedicated roster pop-up.
expectations: Hacking rules and automatic gameplay effects remain unchanged by this attribute-storage feature.
approach: Extend the version-1 player-config and private desktop protobuf contracts, normalize legacy field absence at strict adapters, and keep all roster mutations revision-conditional, inactive-only, persistence-first coordinator transitions. Replace inline durable roster editing with an authoritative modal dialog while keeping attributes private from players and gameplay.

decisions.decision: Keep player-config JSON at version 1 with strict presence-aware legacy defaults
decisions.why: The new attributes are additive and canonical domain values must never treat explicit invalid zero or null as absence
decisions.rejected: A version-2 document or domain-level zero default

decisions.decision: Add persistence fields 3 and 4 with optional presence and private projection fields 4 and 5
decisions.why: Presence preserves legacy semantics without renumbering and master projections remain canonical
decisions.rejected: Field reuse or publishing attributes in the public player schema

decisions.decision: Track an exact player-config content digest and refuse stale external replacements
decisions.why: A deterministic digest prevents silently recreating or overwriting a file changed while the dialog is open
decisions.rejected: Timestamp checks, file watchers, or platform-specific cross-process locks

decisions.decision: Require expected coordination revision and no active broadcast inside every roster mutation transaction
decisions.why: One authoritative guard prevents duplicate, stale, and live-session changes before allocation or persistence
decisions.rejected: UI-only disabling or a separate replay cache

decisions.decision: Submit one complete player profile and replace the Wails rename method with update
decisions.why: Atomic full-profile persistence avoids partial revisions while the compatible protobuf container retains published field identity
decisions.rejected: Separate attribute mutations or dual live rename/update paths

decisions.decision: Use an in-page HTML dialog and keep live assignment controls in logical-session management
decisions.why: This matches the existing single-window architecture and preserves broadcast-scoped correction while durable editing is read-only
decisions.rejected: A second Wails window or disabling established assignment correction

decisions.decision: Keep Intelligence and Hacker availability master-private and add no dependencies
decisions.why: The approved scope is storage and master management, and existing generated-contract, modal, persistence, and test tooling is sufficient
decisions.rejected: Public player fields, automatic hacking effects, or new state/UI libraries

plan.summary: Planned a backward-compatible, atomic roster-profile extension with inactive-only modal management.
plan.key_finding: The coordinator already persists candidate rosters before publication, so the feature can preserve atomicity by adding revision, broadcast, and file-digest guards around that existing path.
